Lexirise shared components

React/TypeScript library providing the settings panel, reader, lookup window, types and capabilities used by both applications.

  1. This is a developer library, not a third standalone web app. End users get it through the Emulingo and toolkit installers. No game files or API credentials are needed here.
  2. For contributing: download the source ZIP or clone the public repository. Install Node.js 24. From the source folder run npm run setup, or double-click Install.cmd on Windows. This installs locked dependencies and checks/builds the library.
  3. For another React application: download the verified release .tgz, then use npm install /path/to/firebird55-lexirise-components-VERSION.tgz in that application. React and React DOM are peer dependencies. Import @firebird55/lexirise-components and its styles.css; provide your own transport, storage and popup portal.
  4. For the two existing applications, edit shared source here, publish a release, then run npm run shared:update -- --version <version> --all from the shared source checkout. Both sibling consumer folders are checked and their generated pinned imports committed.
  5. Read AGENTS.md and RELEASE.md before making changes. Never edit a consumer's vendor/lexirise-components directory manually.

Local data and game files

Package installation into another host is an explicit developer action. Credentials are supplied only by the host adapter. Source ZIPs include the developer installer and contribution instructions; the package includes the same agent documentation.

Contributing with an AI agent

Read AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and RELEASE.md before making changes. Inspect Git status, preserve unrelated work and local data, commit completed logical changes and run checks before pushing. Shared UI is edited only in the shared source repository, then released and synchronized into both apps. Never edit generated vendor copies.

Use npm run lexirise:watch to review upstream changes and npm run release -- --version <semver> for authorized releases. Verify hosted Actions, downloaded checksums and provenance. Keep repositories private, account writes mocked, credentials local, and release infrastructure independent of the cluster. Installing this project does not itself authorize an agent to publish or change account settings.
